findings.claim: BlockedEmail.should_block? writes match_count/last_match_at from inside validation, so the block stats are wrong: an increment made inside save/save! is rolled back when validation fails (Rails 3.2 with_transaction_returning_status), so blocked attempts via User.create_for_email and EmailToken.confirm are never counted; UsersController#create counts only because of the separate user.valid? call before user.save; :do_nothing matches are counted twice per signup (valid? + save). The query-named method hides a DB write.
findings.evidence: lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13 calls should_block? during validation; blocked_email.rb:13-17 does match_count += 1; save; users_controller.rb:166-172 calls user.valid? then user.save; user.rb:102 create_for_email uses save!; email_token.rb confirm wraps save! in User.transaction and rescues RecordInvalid. Reasoned from Rails 3.2.12 semantics, not executed. Proposed red test: POST users#create with a :do_nothing BlockedEmail and expect match_count to change by 1 (patch gives 2); User.create_for_email on a blocked address then expect match_count == 1 (patch gives 0 outside transactional fixtures).
findings.reason: Breaks the commit's stated goal of tracking how often each address is blocked. Three correctness-relevant seats raised it independently with consistent call-path evidence. Fix: move the stat update out of the validator, or make it an atomic update outside the user's save transaction.

findings.claim: The block lookup is case-sensitive and nothing is normalised, so changing letter case bypasses the block (bad@spammers.org blocked, Bad@spammers.org or bad@SPAMMERS.org allowed).
findings.evidence: BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first is an exact = match on Postgres; User.new_from_params (user.rb:87) assigns params[:email] raw with no downcase; the domain whitelist/blacklist in the same validator uses a case-insensitive Regexp. Reasoned. Red test: Fabricate(:blocked_email, email: 'bad@spammers.org'); BlockedEmail.should_block?('Bad@spammers.org').should be_true (fails on patch).
findings.reason: Security bypass of the feature's core purpose. Trivially reproducible as a model spec. Normalise on store and on lookup (lower(email)).

findings.claim: The EmailValidator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block?, a class this patch owns, and no integration or controller test covers the blocked-signup path, the stats persisting through a real User#save, case handling, or the new errors/values JSON keys. This is why the stats and case bugs went unseen.
findings.evidence: email_validator_spec.rb:11,17 stub should_block?; blocked_email_spec.rb calls should_block? directly outside any save and uses only lowercase emails; there is no controller spec for users#create errors/values and nothing under test/javascripts for rejectedEmails. This breaches the documented 'never mock things you own' rule and CONTRIBUTING.md 'Include tests'.
findings.reason: The integration tests that would guard the two Important fixes above are the same tests that close this gap. Replace the stub with a fabricated BlockedEmail row.

findings.claim: The counter update is read-modify-write (match_count += 1; save), so concurrent attempts lose increments; the save return value is ignored, and save re-runs the uniqueness SELECT.
findings.evidence: blocked_email.rb:14-16. Atomic alternative: BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now]).
findings.reason: Falls out of the stats-in-validation fix at no extra cost; the same update_all resolves both.

findings.claim: The file has no trailing newline.
findings.evidence: The patch shows '\ No newline at end of file'; every other file in the repo ends with a newline.

findings.claim: Any server-side email error, including 'has already been taken' and domain whitelist/blacklist, adds the address to rejectedEmails, and the field then shows the generic user.email.invalid text instead of the server's reason. The list lasts until page reload, so an address unblocked in the meantime cannot be retried.
findings.evidence: create_account_controller.js:69-74 (emailValidation uses I18n user.email.invalid) and 274-276 (pushes on any result.errors.email).
findings.reason: ponytail: UX wording only. Blocking resubmission of a rejected address is still correct, and showing the server's message is a separate small change.

findings.claim: Blocking applies to any email change, not just signup: change_email never checks the blocklist and sends a confirmation to the blocked address, then EmailToken.confirm hits RecordInvalid, rescues it and returns nil, so the user gets a generic token failure with no reason.
findings.evidence: users_controller.rb:265-286 change_email; email_token.rb confirm rescues ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid; the validator runs on email_changed? (user.rb:47).
findings.reason: ponytail: scope question (superpowers judged email-change blocking intentional). Better error surfacing is a follow-up and needs product intent.

findings.claim: Invite redemption to a blocked email (User.create_for_email with save!) raises an unhandled ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.
findings.evidence: user.rb:102 save!; the domain blacklist already behaved this way, and this adds a second trigger.
findings.reason: ponytail: pre-existing failure mode (domain blacklist) that this patch only extends. Handle it with the invite flow.

findings.claim: The :do_nothing action type (enum, NOT NULL action_type column, set_defaults callback, fabricator line, two spec contexts) has no producer in the patch: no admin UI, caller or setting.
findings.evidence: A grep of app/lib/config finds no use of do_nothing or BlockedEmail.actions outside the model; the commit message only asks to block.
findings.reason: ponytail: advisory over-engineering. It is likely groundwork for a watch-only mode, and removing it now churns the migration. Revisit if no producer lands.

findings.claim: match_count/last_match_at also increment for :do_nothing matches, while the commit says it tracks how many times each address is blocked.
findings.evidence: blocked_email.rb:13-14 increments before checking action_type; spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:42-44 asserts that do_nothing matches are counted.
findings.reason: ponytail: the specs make the behaviour deliberate, so this is a commit-message/naming mismatch, not a defect.

findings.claim: values: user.attributes.slice('name','username','email') is redundant: the client reads only values.email, which equals the email it already submitted, because new_from_params does not normalise it.
findings.evidence: create_account_controller.js:274-276 reads only result.values.email; the email variable is captured at line 262; user.rb:87 assigns params[:email] raw.
findings.reason: ponytail: advisory cleanup. If email normalisation is added by the case-sensitivity fix, the echo becomes meaningful, so decide after that fix.

findings.claim: The 'last_match_at is null' example tests an ActiveRecord/migration default, not app logic.
findings.evidence: blocked_email_spec.rb:12-16 checks that a fresh row has a nil nullable column; documented standard: never test framework code.
findings.reason: ponytail: harmless spec noise. Drop it when the spec is reworked for the stats fix.

findings.claim: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) sits on the class prototype, so all controller instances share it.
findings.reason: Both raising seats state it is harmless because the controller is an Ember singleton; there is no failure scenario in this codebase.

findings.claim: errors: user.errors.to_hash exposes every attribute error as structured JSON, while the client only needs email.
findings.reason: The response goes only to the requester and holds validation messages for their own submitted input (open-code-review explicitly found no security issue in the new fields); no information leaks.
